payload.throughline: Trace route, driving pressure, exchange surface, circulating component, and carriage form before predicting where material moves.

learner_content_blocks: Low-stakes check: trace one chamber-to-vessel transition. It neither selects a route nor awards exit credit.
Right heart sends blood to lungs; left heart sends blood to systemic tissues. Arteries go away and veins return.
Systemic veins → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary arteries → lungs.
Pulmonary veins → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta; systole is contraction peak and diastole relaxation low.
Use two loops joined in series through a four-chamber pump.
I name vessels by direction, not oxygen shortcut, then map contraction or relaxation to pressure.
Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood away from heart.
Diastolic pressure corresponds to ventricular relaxation.
Trace arrows before naming oxygen state.
Use away versus toward.
Relate cardiac state to pressure.
Pulmonary vessels break the artery-equals-oxygen shortcut.
Near exit: classify a pulmonary vessel.
Changed exit: map relaxation to pressure.
Repair vessel naming by direction.
Freshly classify a pulmonary vessel.
Repair systole/diastole mapping.
Freshly map relaxation.
Trace two loops; name vessels by direction and pressure by cardiac state.
Low-stakes check: match vessel structure to pressure, flow, or exchange. It neither selects a route nor awards exit credit.
Arteries handle higher pressure, veins return and store volume, and capillaries exchange across thin endothelium.
Flow rises with pressure difference and falls with resistance; smaller radius strongly raises resistance.
Cutaneous dilation raises skin flow and heat loss; constriction conserves heat.
Use pump conduit, return reservoir, and exchange sheet.
I hold pressure or resistance constant before predicting flow.
Narrower arteriole raises resistance.
Thin capillary endothelium shortens diffusion distance.
Name pressure role or exchange role.
Change one flow variable.
Select a vessel feature.
Capillary exchange area is collective; one capillary is narrow.
Near exit: predict pressure-driven flow.
Changed exit: relate skin caliber to heat.
Repair resistance direction.
Freshly predict narrowing.
Repair skin-flow response.
Freshly predict cold constriction.
Structure sets pressure tolerance, return, exchange, resistance, and thermal flow.
Low-stakes check: separate plasma from formed elements. It neither selects a route nor awards exit credit.
Whole blood combines plasma, erythrocytes, leukocytes, and platelets in a regulated circulating volume.
Plasma carries dissolved chemicals; erythrocytes carry hemoglobin; leukocytes defend; platelets support hemostasis.
Marrow production and removal of aged cells including in spleen maintain erythrocyte turnover; water/solute balance regulates plasma volume.
Use liquid medium, formed elements, life-cycle turnover, and volume control.
I distinguish cell count from plasma volume and production from removal.
Cell-free upper liquid is plasma.
Marrow-to-spleen tracing shows erythrocyte turnover.
Match component to function.
Trace both turnover directions.
Define whole blood.
Do not replace the bounded model with a disease catalog.
Near exit: predict plasma-volume change.
Changed exit: trace cell turnover.
Repair liquid-versus-cell distinction.
Freshly identify plasma.
Repair both turnover directions.
Freshly trace turnover.
Plasma carries, cells specialize, marrow and spleen turn over erythrocytes, and water balance sets volume.
Low-stakes check: order platelet plug and fibrin stabilization. It neither selects a route nor awards exit credit.
Coagulation is a local bounded protective response that limits blood loss without a full factor catalog.
Platelets adhere and aggregate at injury.
Plasma coagulation reactions generate fibrin that stabilizes the plug; localization and later resolution preserve flow.
Patch first, reinforce second, contain the repair, then restore the route.
I separate initiating platelets from later fibrin and trapped erythrocytes.
Adhesion failure impairs initial plug.
Fibrin failure leaves a weak plug.
Order stages.
State why the response is bounded.
Distinguish trapped cells.
Global clot spread is not protective hemostasis.
Near exit: predict platelet failure.
Changed exit: predict fibrin failure.
Repair stage order.
Freshly identify platelet stage.
Repair localization and resolution.
Freshly identify bounded repair.
Platelets plug, fibrin stabilizes, and bounded resolution preserves circulation.
Low-stakes check: separate content, partial pressure, affinity, and carriage form. It neither selects a route nor awards exit credit.
Most oxygen is hemoglobin-bound; most carbon dioxide is bicarbonate; dissolved oxygen sets partial pressure.
Hematocrit and hemoglobin affect oxygen capacity at a given saturation.
Higher tissue CO2/acidity favors unloading; lungs load oxygen and unload carbon dioxide.
Track gas, carriage form, compartment, and tissue-versus-lung direction.
I do not equate dissolved oxygen pressure with total hemoglobin-bound content.
Less hemoglobin lowers content at unchanged dissolved oxygen.
Bicarbonate is the largest CO2 pool.
Rank carriage forms.
Relate hematocrit to capacity.
Predict affinity change.
Detailed neural/endocrine control and clinical blood-gas management remain bounded external parameters.

Changed exit: track both gases in lungs.
Repair dissolved-versus-bound oxygen.
Freshly predict lower hemoglobin content.
Repair CO2 form ranking.
Freshly predict tissue unloading.
Hemoglobin carries oxygen, bicarbonate carries most CO2, and local conditions tune affinity.
